subject: Private Control Plane identity contract: SAML assertion schema, role-binding conventions, and SCIM reconciliation
messages:
From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@edgesecure.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: priya.shah@priuscloud.com
Date: 2027-01-18T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP identity kickoff — short checklist

Hey Tessa,

Thanks for the quick call this morning. As discussed, EdgeSecure is moving to a Private Control-Plane hosted in our VPC and we need to lock the identity contract before we begin the deployment sprint. High-level asks from our security team:

- A precise SAML assertion schema (attribute names/types, required vs optional) so our IdP mapping can be tested in staging.
- Guidance on how Redwood expects role bindings to look (service-account vs user-level bindings) for delegated admin scenarios.
- A SCIM backfill plan — we currently have ~1.2k users and several groups we want to sync into the Private CP.

Can you share a concrete example assertion and the minimal attribute set Redwood needs to reconstruct identity+entitlements? Also whether we should send group claims or perform SCIM-exclusive group provisioning.

Marcus
Director of Platform Security
EdgeSecure Inc.

Attachments: none
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@edgesecure.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-18T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP identity kickoff — short checklist

Marcus — great to sync earlier. Summary and proposal below.

1) Minimal SAML assertion (proposal)
- NameID: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress (primary identifier)
- Attributes to include (keys we expect):
  - email (String, required)
  - given_name (String, optional)
  - family_name (String, optional)
  - uid (String, optional) — your internal immutable id if available
  - groups (Array of String, optional) — format: <group-path> or <org>/<team>
  - roles (Array of String, optional) — Redwood role names for direct binding (see matrix)
  - assertion_issued_at (ISO8601, required) — for replay protection

We recommend sending both email and a stable uid when possible; email alone is okay for most workflows but uid prevents issues when an email changes.

2) Role-binding conventions (how Redwood will map assertions)
- Preferred: SCIM group -> Redwood role mapping. This is authoritative for access control.
- Fallback: SAML roles attribute can contain explicit Redwood role names; Redwood will accept these for cross-environment fallbacks (useful for quick POC).
- Service accounts: represented as SCIM Users with a service-account flag; recommended to create dedicated SCIM users for machine principals.

3) SCIM backfill and reconciliation plan (high level)
- Step A (dry run): customer exports user list + group membership CSV; our team runs a simulated import in staging and shares reconciliation report.
- Step B (SCIM push): initial bulk create via SCIM bulk endpoint; Redwood returns per-user status and id mapping.
- Step C (reconcile): run daily reconcile job for 7 days to pick up delta mismatches, then move to real-time sync.

4) Minimal test vectors and timeline
- We'll need at least 10 test users with variegated membership (multi-group, email-change case, service-account).
- Proposed timeline: staging assertion contract by 2027-01-21, SCIM dry-run by 2027-01-25.

I attached a first-draft assertion contract and a role-binding matrix template for your team to fill. Can you confirm who on your IdP side will own the mapping and whether you prefer groups-in-assertion vs SCIM-only groups?

Thanks — looped in Aditya for product-level constraints and Laura for deployment handoff.

--
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Email: tessa.morgan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134
Redwood Inference
Attachments: saml-assertion-contract-v1.docx, role-binding-matrix.csv
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-18T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP identity kickoff — implementation notes

Quick internal notes on integration constraints:

- Audit / logging: we must persist original assertion payload (redacted for PII) for 90 days for troubleshooting and audit; ensure EdgeSecure is aware of log retention expectations.
- SCIM rate limits: initial backfill will hit higher throughput; we should whitelist their control-plane host for temporary rate bump (coord with infra ops).
- Role entropy: avoid pushing arbitrary strings in roles claim — we will canonicalize only names listed in the role-binding CSV. Extra values are ignored but logged as warnings.

Laura — for the deployment runbook, we need an ops checklist that includes: pre-seed SCIM ids, test assertion snapshots, and a rollback plan if SCIM bulk fails (backout action: mark newly created users inactive and notify).

Rishi — please advise if there are any enforcement differences for on-prem private CP vs Redwood Hosted; specifically whether we need to gate SCIM writes behind a specific control-plane feature flag.

- Aditya
Product Lead, Private Deployments
From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@edgesecure.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: priya.shah@priuscloud.com
Date: 2027-01-19T08:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP identity kickoff — short checklist

Thanks, Tessa — this is very helpful. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Our IdP team prefers groups-in-assertion for faster cutover. They can include groups as array claims but would prefer not to run SCIM for the first sprint. Is that acceptable as a temporary pattern?
- We will provide a stable uid for all users.
- Attached: our IdP metadata (cert + issuer) and an export of group paths for the 1.2k users. We'll request a rate bump for the SCIM endpoint for the initial sync window.

One more ask: can Redwood provide an example SAML assertion that includes nested group paths and a service-account example? That will help our mapping rules.

Marcus

Attachments: edgesecure-idp-metadata.xml, edgesecure-groups-export.csv

Subject: Re: Private CP identity kickoff — acceptance & next steps

Marcus — excellent, thank you for the metadata and the group export. Next steps and action owners:

1) Tessa (Redwood SE) — produce a sample SAML assertion JSON and a service-account example (by 2027-01-21). See attached: saml-assertion-contract-v1.docx (contains sample assertion and required/optional attribute table).
2) EdgeSecure IdP (Marcus/Priya) — confirm whether groups-in-assertion will use full path values or short team names; fill the role-binding-matrix.csv with 5 representative mappings we can test (by 2027-01-23).
3) Aditya (Product) — define whether feature flag gating is necessary for SCIM writes; will respond by 2027-01-22.
4) Laura (Deployments) — produce a runbook stub for SCIM backfill + rollback; include log collection and 90-day retention note (by 2027-01-24).

I will schedule a 45-minute follow-up to review the sample assertion and one end-to-end user creation in staging next week.

If EdgeSecure is comfortable with groups-in-assertion for cutover, we'll treat SCIM as the canonical source after the initial sync (we'll run reconciliation as described).

Thanks all — will upload the doc and matrix to the Drive link and post a short summary to the HubSpot ticket.

--
